module_title: Advanced Regulations, Circuit Breakers, and Trading Mechanisms
introduction: This advanced level focuses on the highly technical safety mechanisms built into the stock market to prevent crashes, the modern settlement cycles, and illegal trading practices.

core_concepts.title: Circuit Breakers
core_concepts.description: A mechanism implemented by SEBI to prevent market crashes due to panic selling. If the market index (Sensex/Nifty) falls or rises too rapidly by a specific percentage (10%, 15%, 20%), trading is automatically 'halted' for a specific duration to let the market cool down.

core_concepts.title: T+1 Settlement Cycle
core_concepts.description: India is the second country in the world (after China) to move to a T+1 settlement cycle. If you buy or sell a share today ('Trade Day' or 'T'), the shares or the money will be credited to your account on the very next working day (+1).

core_concepts.title: Insider Trading
core_concepts.description: A strictly illegal practice. It occurs when a corporate insider (like a CEO, director, or employee) buys or sells their company's stock based on 'Material Non-Public Information' (secret information that regular investors don't know). SEBI aggressively prosecutes this.

core_concepts.title: Demat Account and Depositories
core_concepts.description: Shares are no longer kept as physical paper certificates. They are held electronically in a 'Dematerialized' (Demat) account. In India, this digital vault service is provided by two central depositories: NSDL and CDSL.

important_entities.name: India VIX (Volatility Index)
important_entities.significance: VIX measures the degree of fluctuation (volatility) expected by traders over the next 30 days. If the VIX is high, it indicates extreme fear, panic, and rapid price changes in the market.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: NSDL was promoted primarily by the National Stock Exchange (NSE), whereas CDSL was promoted by the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). While you can use either for any trade today, knowing their origin is a niche exam question.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: T+1 simply means next-day delivery of cash or shares.

exam_strategy_tips: Terms like 'Insider Trading', 'Front Running', and 'Circuit Breakers' are critical for UPSC Prelims and NISM certifications. Always associate these regulatory terms directly with SEBI's mandate.
